question_text: What is the purpose of the HTML <!DOCTYPE html> declaration?
expected_answer: <!DOCTYPE html> tells the browser to render the page in standards mode using HTML5, preventing quirks mode which causes inconsistent rendering across browsers.

question_text: What is the difference between HTML head and body sections?
expected_answer: The <head> contains metadata (title, meta tags, link to CSS, scripts). The <body> contains all visible page content (text, images, forms). Only body content is rendered visually.

question_text: What are semantic HTML elements and why are they important?
expected_answer: Semantic elements like <header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <article>, <aside>, <footer> convey meaning about their content, improving accessibility, SEO, and code readability over generic <div> elements.

question_text: What is the difference between <section> and <article> in HTML5?
expected_answer: <article> is self-contained, independently distributable content (blog post, news article). <section> is a thematic grouping of content with no meaning outside the page. Articles can contain sections.

question_text: What is the role of the <nav> element?
expected_answer: <nav> wraps a set of navigation links (site navigation, table of contents). Only major navigation blocks should use <nav>; footer links may not require it. Helps screen readers skip navigation.

question_text: What is the difference between <header> and <h1> in HTML?
expected_answer: <header> is a structural element containing introductory content (logo, navigation, h1). <h1> is a heading tag for the main page title. A page can have multiple <header> elements but best practice limits <h1> to one.

question_text: What is the difference between inline, block, and inline-block display values?
expected_answer: block: starts new line, full width. inline: flows in text, no width/height. inline-block: flows in text but accepts width, height, and vertical padding like a block element.

question_text: What is the HTML5 <figure> and <figcaption> element?
expected_answer: <figure> wraps self-contained media content (image, diagram, code). <figcaption> provides a caption for it. Their relationship is semantic and accessible without relying on nearby text.

question_text: How do you make a link open in a new tab and why is rel='noopener noreferrer' important?
expected_answer: Use target='_blank' to open in new tab. rel='noopener' prevents the new page from accessing the opener via window.opener (security). noreferrer also hides the referrer header.

question_text: What is the difference between the <button> element and an <input type='submit'>?
expected_answer: <button> is more flexible: it can contain HTML (icons + text), has type (submit/reset/button), and is styled more easily. <input type='submit'> is a void element accepting only value text.

question_text: What is the tabindex attribute and how does it affect keyboard navigation?
expected_answer: tabindex controls focus order: tabindex=0 adds to natural tab order, tabindex=-1 removes from tab order but allows programmatic focus, positive values set explicit order (avoid unless necessary).

question_text: What is the difference between <script>, <script defer>, and <script async>?
expected_answer: Normal <script> blocks HTML parsing. defer downloads asynchronously, executes after DOM parsed in order. async downloads asynchronously, executes as soon as available regardless of DOM or order.

question_text: What are ARIA roles and why are they used?
expected_answer: ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) roles define the purpose of elements to assistive technologies when HTML semantics are insufficient: role='dialog', role='button', role='alert'.

question_text: What is aria-label vs aria-labelledby?
expected_answer: aria-label provides a text label directly. aria-labelledby references the ID of another element that serves as the label. aria-labelledby is preferred when visible text exists.

question_text: What is aria-hidden and when should it be used?
expected_answer: aria-hidden='true' hides elements from assistive technologies. Use on purely decorative elements (icons), or when content is visually hidden but not meant for screen readers.

question_text: What is the srcset attribute in the tag?
expected_answer: srcset provides multiple image sources with width descriptors (w) or density descriptors (x) so the browser picks the most appropriate image for the device: srcset='img-320.jpg 320w, img-640.jpg 640w'.

question_text: What is the sizes attribute in HTML images?
expected_answer: sizes works with srcset to tell the browser how wide the image will be at different viewport sizes before layout is calculated, enabling better resource selection: sizes='(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 50vw'.

question_text: What is the difference between the <link> and <a> elements?
expected_answer: <link> (in <head>) defines relationships between the document and external resources (CSS, icons, preload). <a> creates hyperlinks within the page content for user navigation.

question_text: What is the HTML5 input type='range'?
expected_answer: input type='range' renders a slider control for selecting a numeric value within a min-max range, with step attribute for increment size. Value accessed via JavaScript or form submission.

question_text: What are the global HTML attributes?
expected_answer: Global attributes apply to any HTML element: id, class, style, title, hidden, tabindex, contenteditable, draggable, data-*, lang, dir, slot, part.

question_text: What is the contenteditable attribute?
expected_answer: contenteditable='true' makes any element's content editable by the user in the browser, similar to a text editor. Used for rich text editors and inline content editing.

question_text: What is the difference between display:none, visibility:hidden, and opacity:0?
expected_answer: display:none removes from layout (no space, hidden from AT). visibility:hidden hides visually but keeps space, still accessible. opacity:0 hides visually but keeps space and is interactive.

question_text: What is the CSS box-sizing property?
expected_answer: box-sizing: content-box (default) excludes padding and border from width. box-sizing: border-box includes them, making layout calculations intuitive. Apply * { box-sizing: border-box } globally.

question_text: What is CSS specificity and how do you calculate it?
expected_answer: Specificity: inline (1,0,0,0), ID (0,1,0,0), class/attribute/pseudo-class (0,0,1,0), element/pseudo-element (0,0,0,1). Compare left to right; !important overrides all.

question_text: What is the difference between CSS class selector and attribute selector?
expected_answer: .class targets elements with that class attribute. [attr] targets any element with the specified attribute, with modifiers: [attr='value'] exact match, [attr^='val'] starts with, [attr*='val'] contains.

question_text: What is the CSS :root pseudo-class?
expected_answer: :root selects the root element of the document (html element), with higher specificity than html selector. Commonly used to declare CSS custom properties (variables) for global scope.

question_text: What is the difference between max-width and min-width in CSS?
expected_answer: max-width sets the maximum size (element shrinks below this but never grows beyond). min-width sets the minimum size (element grows beyond this but never shrinks below). Both are used for responsive layouts.

question_text: What is CSS Flexbox and what problem does it solve?
expected_answer: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout model solving alignment, distribution, and ordering of items within a container. It replaces float-based layouts with predictable, flexible item arrangement.

question_text: What is the difference between justify-content and align-items in Flexbox?
expected_answer: justify-content aligns items along the main axis (horizontal in row). align-items aligns items along the cross axis (vertical in row). flex-direction changes which axis is main.

question_text: What is flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis?
expected_answer: flex-grow: how much the item grows relative to others when extra space. flex-shrink: how much it shrinks when short of space. flex-basis: initial size before growing/shrinking. Shorthand: flex: grow shrink basis.

question_text: What is the align-self property in Flexbox?
expected_answer: align-self overrides the parent's align-items for an individual flex item, allowing one item to be aligned differently from the rest on the cross axis.

question_text: What is the order property in Flexbox?
expected_answer: The order property controls visual display order of flex items without changing DOM order. Items with lower order values appear first; default is 0. Should be used carefully for accessibility.

question_text: What is CSS Grid and how do you define a grid?
expected_answer: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system. Define a grid with display:grid and grid-template-columns/rows: grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) creates 3 equal columns.

question_text: What is the fr unit in CSS Grid?
expected_answer: fr (fractional unit) represents a fraction of the available space in the grid container. grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr creates two columns where the second is twice the first.

question_text: What is grid-template-areas in CSS?
expected_answer: grid-template-areas assigns named areas to grid cells using a visual ASCII-art-like syntax, then items are placed with grid-area: header, enabling clear and readable layout definitions.

question_text: What is the difference between grid-column and grid-area?
expected_answer: grid-column sets column span (grid-column: 1 / 3 spans from line 1 to 3). grid-area sets both row and column: grid-area: row-start / col-start / row-end / col-end or a named area.

question_text: What is the repeat() function in CSS Grid?
expected_answer: repeat(count, size) simplifies repeating column/row definitions: repeat(4, 1fr) creates 4 equal columns. repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr)) creates responsive columns.

question_text: What is the minmax() function in CSS Grid?
expected_answer: minmax(min, max) defines a size range for a grid track: minmax(200px, 1fr) means the column is at least 200px but grows up to fill available space, enabling responsive layouts.

question_text: What is the CSS position: sticky?
expected_answer: position: sticky is a hybrid between relative and fixed. The element scrolls normally until it reaches the threshold (e.g., top: 0), then sticks in place within its parent container.

question_text: What is the difference between position: relative and position: absolute?
expected_answer: relative offsets from normal position but keeps its space in flow. absolute removes from flow, positions relative to nearest non-static ancestor (or initial containing block if none).

question_text: How do you vertically and horizontally center an element in CSS?
expected_answer: Flexbox: parent { display:flex; justify-content:center; align-items:center }. Grid: parent { display:grid; place-items:center }. Absolute: top:50%;left:50%;transform:translate(-50%,-50%).

question_text: What are CSS media queries and how are they written?
expected_answer: @media (condition) { rules } applies CSS conditionally: @media (max-width: 768px) { .nav { display:none } }. Can target width, height, orientation, resolution, and hover capability.

question_text: What is mobile-first vs desktop-first CSS approach?
expected_answer: Mobile-first uses min-width queries, starting with small screen styles and adding complexity for larger screens. Desktop-first uses max-width queries. Mobile-first is preferred for performance.

question_text: What are CSS custom properties (variables) and how do they work?
expected_answer: Defined with -- prefix: --primary: #333; used with var(): color: var(--primary). Cascade and inherit like regular properties. Scoped to :root for global, or element for local use.

question_text: What is the CSS float property and its modern use cases?
expected_answer: float was historically used for layouts (now replaced by Flexbox/Grid). Modern uses: wrapping text around images (float:left/right on img), clearfix for containing floated children.

question_text: What is a clearfix in CSS?
expected_answer: Clearfix forces a parent to contain its floated children by adding a pseudo-element: .clearfix::after { content:''; display:table; clear:both }. Prevents parent height collapse.

question_text: What is the CSS overflow property and its values?
expected_answer: overflow controls how content that exceeds its container is handled: visible (default, overflows), hidden (clips), scroll (always shows scrollbar), auto (scrollbar only when needed).

question_text: What is the difference between text-overflow:ellipsis and word-break?
expected_answer: text-overflow:ellipsis (needs overflow:hidden + white-space:nowrap) truncates overflowing text with '...'. word-break controls line breaks within words: break-all breaks at any character.

question_text: What is the CSS transition timing function?
expected_answer: Timing functions control animation speed curve: ease (default), linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, and cubic-bezier(x1,y1,x2,y2) for custom curves. steps() for frame-based animation.

question_text: What is the CSS transform-origin property?
expected_answer: transform-origin sets the pivot point for CSS transforms. Default is center (50% 50%). Changing it to top-left (0 0) or custom values affects how rotate/scale transforms appear.

question_text: What are CSS keyframe animations?
expected_answer: @keyframes defines animation steps; animation property applies it: @keyframes slide { from { transform:translateX(-100%) } to { transform:translateX(0) } } animation: slide 0.3s ease-in.

question_text: What is the CSS animation-fill-mode property?
expected_answer: animation-fill-mode controls element style before/after animation: none (default), forwards (keeps end state), backwards (applies start state during delay), both (combines forwards+backwards).

question_text: What is CSS object-position?
expected_answer: object-position works with object-fit to control the focal point of an image/video within its container box, similar to background-position for replaced elements.

question_text: What is the CSS background shorthand?
expected_answer: background shorthand: background: color image repeat attachment position/size. Example: background: #fff url('img.jpg') no-repeat center/cover. Multiple backgrounds separated by comma.

question_text: What is the CSS background-size cover vs contain?
expected_answer: cover scales image to fill container (may crop). contain scales to fit entirely within container (may show empty space). Both maintain aspect ratio.

question_text: What are CSS gradients?
expected_answer: CSS gradients create smooth color transitions: linear-gradient(direction, color1, color2), radial-gradient(shape, color1, color2), conic-gradient(). Used as background-image values.

question_text: What is the CSS filter property?
expected_answer: filter applies visual effects to elements: blur(px), brightness(%), contrast(%), grayscale(%), hue-rotate(deg), invert(%), opacity(%), saturate(%), sepia(%), drop-shadow().

question_text: What is the CSS mix-blend-mode property?
expected_answer: mix-blend-mode controls how an element's content blends with its background: multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten, difference, etc. Used for creative layering effects.

question_text: What is the CSS appearance property?
expected_answer: appearance: none removes native browser styling from form elements (buttons, selects, checkboxes), allowing full custom styling while maintaining the element's semantic behavior.

question_text: What is the CSS pointer-events property?
expected_answer: pointer-events:none makes an element unresponsive to mouse/touch events (clicks pass through). Useful for overlay elements that should not intercept events below them.

question_text: What is the CSS user-select property?
expected_answer: user-select controls whether text in an element can be selected by the user: none (prevent selection), text (allow), all (select all on single click). Useful for buttons and UI elements.

question_text: What is the CSS cursor property?
expected_answer: cursor changes the mouse cursor when hovering: pointer (hand for links/buttons), default, text, grab, grabbing, crosshair, not-allowed, zoom-in. Provides UX feedback about interactivity.

question_text: What is the CSS outline property and how does it differ from border?
expected_answer: outline draws outside the border, not affecting layout (no space taken). Used for focus indicators. Unlike border, outline doesn't affect the box model. Never remove outline without a replacement for accessibility.

question_text: What is the CSS :focus-visible pseudo-class?
expected_answer: :focus-visible applies focus styles only when the element is focused via keyboard (not mouse click), enabling visible keyboard focus rings without showing them for mouse users.

question_text: What is the CSS scroll-behavior property?
expected_answer: scroll-behavior: smooth enables smooth animated scrolling for anchor link navigation and JavaScript scroll calls (window.scrollTo). Default is auto (instant jump).

question_text: What is the CSS scroll-snap property?
expected_answer: scroll-snap-type on container and scroll-snap-align on items create snap points for carousels/sliders, ensuring content snaps to defined positions during scroll without JavaScript.

question_text: What is the CSS writing-mode property?
expected_answer: writing-mode controls text direction: horizontal-tb (default), vertical-rl (top to bottom, right to left), vertical-lr. Used for vertical text in East Asian typography.

question_text: What is the CSS counter and counter() function?
expected_answer: CSS counters create auto-incremented numbers for lists or custom numbering: counter-reset on parent, counter-increment on items, counter() or counters() in content property.

question_text: What is JavaScript and how does it relate to the browser?
expected_answer: JavaScript is a single-threaded, event-driven scripting language interpreted by the browser's JS engine (V8, SpiderMonkey). It manipulates the DOM, handles user events, and communicates with servers.

question_text: What are the JavaScript primitive data types?
expected_answer: JavaScript has 7 primitives: string, number, bigint, boolean, undefined, null, and symbol. Primitives are immutable and compared by value. Everything else is an object (reference type).

question_text: What is the difference between null and undefined in JavaScript?
expected_answer: undefined means a variable was declared but not assigned. null is an intentional empty value assigned by code. typeof null === 'object' is a famous JS quirk.

question_text: What is the typeof operator in JavaScript?
expected_answer: typeof returns a string indicating the type: 'string', 'number', 'boolean', 'undefined', 'object' (arrays, null), 'function', 'symbol', 'bigint'.

question_text: What is type coercion in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Type coercion is automatic conversion between types. Implicit: '5' + 3 = '53' (string concat), '5' - 3 = 2 (arithmetic). Explicit: Number(), String(), Boolean(). Use === to avoid coercion bugs.

question_text: What is the difference between var, let, and const in JavaScript?
expected_answer: var is function-scoped and hoisted (initialized as undefined). let and const are block-scoped and not hoisted to usable state (TDZ). const prevents reassignment but not mutation of objects.

question_text: What is variable hoisting in JavaScript?
expected_answer: JavaScript moves var declarations (not initializations) and function declarations to the top of their scope. let/const are in the Temporal Dead Zone until their declaration line is reached.

question_text: What is the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) in JavaScript?
expected_answer: The TDZ is the period between entering a block scope and the actual let/const declaration. Accessing the variable in this zone throws a ReferenceError.

question_text: What is scope in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Scope determines variable accessibility. Global scope: accessible everywhere. Function scope: inside functions only. Block scope: inside {} for let/const. JavaScript uses lexical (static) scoping.

question_text: What is the IIFE (Immediately Invoked Function Expression)?
expected_answer: IIFE is a function that runs immediately after definition: (function() { ... })() or (() => { ... })(). Used to create isolated scope, avoiding global variable pollution.

question_text: What is the JavaScript call stack and how does it work?
expected_answer: The call stack is a LIFO stack tracking function invocations. Each call pushes a frame; each return pops it. Exceeding the max stack depth (infinite recursion) throws 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'.

question_text: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous JavaScript?
expected_answer: Synchronous executes line by line, blocking. Asynchronous (callbacks, Promises, async/await) defers work, freeing the thread to process other tasks while waiting for I/O, timers, or network.

question_text: What is the JavaScript event loop?
expected_answer: The event loop monitors the call stack and task queues. When the call stack is empty, it processes microtasks (Promise callbacks) first, then the task queue (setTimeout callbacks), enabling async behavior.

question_text: What is the difference between setTimeout and setInterval?
expected_answer: setTimeout(fn, delay) executes once after a delay. setInterval(fn, interval) executes repeatedly at the interval. clearTimeout/clearInterval cancel them. Both are minimum delays, not guarantees.

question_text: What is a callback function in JavaScript?
expected_answer: A callback is a function passed as an argument to another function to be called later. Used in event listeners, setTimeout, array methods (map, filter), and async operations.

question_text: What is callback hell and how is it avoided?
expected_answer: Callback hell is deeply nested callbacks making code unreadable. Avoided by: named functions, Promises (chaining .then()), or async/await for flat, readable asynchronous code.

question_text: What is a Promise in JavaScript and what states can it be in?
expected_answer: A Promise represents an eventual value with three states: pending (initial), fulfilled (resolved with value), rejected (failed with reason). Handled via .then(), .catch(), .finally().

question_text: What is the difference between Promise.all() and Promise.allSettled()?
expected_answer: Promise.all() fails fast if any promise rejects. Promise.allSettled() waits for all to complete regardless, returning each result's status and value/reason.

question_text: What is async/await in JavaScript?
expected_answer: async/await is syntactic sugar over Promises. async functions always return a Promise. await pauses execution inside async function until the Promise resolves, enabling synchronous-looking async code.

question_text: How do you handle errors with async/await?
expected_answer: Wrap await expressions in try/catch: try { const data = await fetch(url) } catch(err) { console.error(err) }. Or chain .catch() on the returned Promise.

question_text: What is the DOM and what can JavaScript do with it?
expected_answer: The DOM (Document Object Model) is a tree representation of the HTML document. JavaScript can: query elements, modify content/attributes/styles, create/delete nodes, attach event listeners.

question_text: What are the different ways to select DOM elements in JavaScript?
expected_answer: getElementById (by id), getElementsByClassName/TagName (live HTMLCollection), querySelector (first CSS match), querySelectorAll (all CSS matches, static NodeList).

question_text: What is the difference between NodeList and HTMLCollection?
expected_answer: HTMLCollection is live (updates automatically with DOM changes), only elements. NodeList (from querySelectorAll) is static, contains any node type. Both are array-like but lack full array methods.

question_text: How do you create and append DOM elements in JavaScript?
expected_answer: document.createElement('div') creates an element. element.appendChild(), element.append(), element.insertBefore(), or element.insertAdjacentElement() add it to the DOM.

question_text: What is the difference between innerHTML, textContent, and innerText?
expected_answer: innerHTML sets/gets HTML (XSS risk from user data). textContent sets/gets plain text (no HTML parsing, safe). innerText is like textContent but considers CSS visibility and triggers reflow.

question_text: What is the insertAdjacentHTML method?
expected_answer: insertAdjacentHTML(position, html) inserts HTML relative to an element: beforebegin (before element), afterbegin (first child), beforeend (last child), afterend (after element), without replacing content.

question_text: How do you add and remove CSS classes with JavaScript?
expected_answer: Use classList API: element.classList.add('class'), remove('class'), toggle('class'), contains('class') (returns bool), replace('old','new'). Cleaner than manipulating className string directly.

question_text: What is the difference between getAttribute and element.property in JavaScript?
expected_answer: getAttribute('href') gets the attribute value as written in HTML. element.href returns the resolved property (absolute URL). For boolean attributes (disabled), property is boolean, attribute is string.

question_text: What is the dataset API in JavaScript?
expected_answer: element.dataset accesses data-* attributes as a DOMStringMap. data-user-id='5' becomes element.dataset.userId (camelCase). Provides a structured way to store custom data on elements.

question_text: What is event handling in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Events are triggered by user actions or browser events. Handled via addEventListener(event, callback, options): element.addEventListener('click', handler, { once: true, passive: true }).

question_text: What is event bubbling in JavaScript?
expected_answer: When an event fires on an element, it propagates up through all ancestor elements. A click on a button triggers click handlers on the button, then div, then body, then document.

question_text: What is event delegation and why is it useful?
expected_answer: Attaching a single listener to a parent instead of multiple children, using event.target to identify which child was clicked. More efficient and handles dynamically added elements automatically.

question_text: What is the event.target vs event.currentTarget?
expected_answer: event.target is the element that triggered the event (the actual clicked element). event.currentTarget is the element the listener is attached to (useful in delegation).

question_text: What is event.preventDefault() used for?
expected_answer: Prevents the browser's default action: stops form submission (submit event), link navigation (click on anchor), context menu (contextmenu event), drag default behavior.

question_text: What is the DOMContentLoaded event?
expected_answer: DOMContentLoaded fires when HTML parsing and DOM construction is complete, without waiting for images/stylesheets. Better than window.onload for DOM-manipulation scripts.

question_text: What is the window.onload event?
expected_answer: window.onload fires after the entire page (DOM, images, stylesheets, fonts) has fully loaded. Useful for operations requiring all resources, but usually too late for DOM manipulation.

question_text: What is the JavaScript fetch API?
expected_answer: fetch(url, options) makes HTTP requests returning a Promise. Two-step: first Promise resolves to Response, then .json() or .text() resolves to data. Error handling requires checking response.ok.

question_text: How do you check if a fetch request was successful?
expected_answer: fetch doesn't reject on HTTP error codes (4xx, 5xx). Check response.ok (true for 200-299) or response.status. Throw an error manually for non-ok responses: if (!response.ok) throw new Error().

question_text: What is JSON.stringify() and JSON.parse()?
expected_answer: JSON.stringify() converts JavaScript object to JSON string. JSON.parse() converts JSON string to JavaScript object. stringify accepts replacer and space for formatting; parse accepts reviver for transformation.

question_text: What is local storage and how do you use it?
expected_answer: localStorage.setItem(key, value), getItem(key), removeItem(key), clear(). Only stores strings. Use JSON.stringify/parse for objects. Data persists after browser restart.

question_text: What is the difference between localStorage and sessionStorage?
expected_answer: localStorage persists indefinitely until cleared. sessionStorage is cleared when the tab closes. Both are ~5MB, key-value string storage, not sent to server.

question_text: What is the JavaScript spread operator?
expected_answer: ... expands an iterable into individual elements. Array: [...arr1, ...arr2] merges arrays. Object: {...obj1, ...obj2} shallow-merges objects. Function call: fn(...args) spreads arguments.

question_text: What is destructuring assignment in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Extracts values from arrays/objects into variables. Array: const [a, b] = [1, 2]. Object: const { name, age = 18 } = person. Supports renaming: const { name: fullName } = person.

question_text: What are default function parameters in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Default parameters provide fallback values when arguments are undefined: function greet(name = 'World') { }. Complex expressions are evaluated at call time, not definition time.

question_text: What are template literals in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Template literals use backticks for strings: `Hello ${name}`. Support multi-line strings, expression interpolation, and tagged templates for custom string processing.

question_text: What is object shorthand in ES6?
expected_answer: When property name matches variable name, ES6 shorthand: { name } instead of { name: name }. Method shorthand: { greet() {} } instead of { greet: function() {} }.

question_text: What are computed property names in JavaScript?
expected_answer: ES6 computed properties use [] to define dynamic property keys: { [varName]: value } or { ['key_' + id]: value }, enabling dynamic object creation without post-creation assignment.

question_text: What is the JavaScript Map object and when to use it over an object?
expected_answer: Map allows any type as key, maintains insertion order, has .size property, and is more performant for frequent add/delete. Use over object when keys are non-strings or iteration order matters.

question_text: What is the JavaScript Set object?
expected_answer: Set stores unique values of any type: new Set([1,2,2,3]) → {1,2,3}. Methods: add(), delete(), has(), clear(). Used for deduplication: [...new Set(array)].

question_text: What is a closure in JavaScript and give a real-world use case?
expected_answer: A closure retains access to its outer scope variables. Use case: counter function (private count variable), memoization, event handler factories, module pattern for private state.

question_text: What is the difference between function declaration and function expression?
expected_answer: Function declarations (function fn(){}) are hoisted entirely, callable before definition. Function expressions (const fn = function(){}) are not hoisted to usable state (only variable declaration is).

question_text: What are arrow functions and how do they differ?
expected_answer: Arrow functions (=>) have concise syntax, implicit return for single expressions, and no own this, arguments, or prototype. Cannot be used as constructors. this is inherited lexically.

question_text: What is the this keyword inside an event listener?
expected_answer: In a regular function event listener, this refers to the element the listener is attached to. Arrow functions don't have their own this, so they inherit from the enclosing scope.

question_text: What is bind(), call(), and apply() in JavaScript?
expected_answer: call(thisArg, arg1, arg2) invokes with explicit this and individual args. apply(thisArg, [args]) takes args array. bind(thisArg) returns new bound function without invoking.

question_text: What is the JavaScript prototype?
expected_answer: Every object has a prototype chain (__proto__). When a property is not found on an object, JS looks up the prototype chain. Constructor functions' prototype property defines shared methods.

question_text: What is ES6 class syntax in JavaScript?
expected_answer: class syntax is sugar over prototype-based inheritance: constructor(), methods, static methods, extends for inheritance, super() to call parent. Classes are not hoisted.

question_text: What is the JavaScript module system (ES Modules)?
expected_answer: ES Modules use export (named or default) and import to share code between files. Modules have their own scope, are loaded asynchronously, and execute in strict mode by default.

question_text: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
expected_answer: == does loose comparison with type coercion (1 == '1' is true). === does strict comparison without coercion (1 === '1' is false). Always use === to prevent unexpected coercion bugs.

question_text: What is truthy and falsy in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Falsy values: false, 0, -0, 0n, '' (empty string), null, undefined, NaN. Everything else is truthy. Used in conditional checks and logical operators.

question_text: What is short-circuit evaluation in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Logical operators short-circuit: A && B returns A if falsy, otherwise B. A || B returns A if truthy, otherwise B. A ?? B returns A unless null/undefined, then B.

question_text: What is optional chaining (?.) in JavaScript?
expected_answer: obj?.prop returns undefined (not error) if obj is null/undefined. Works for properties, methods, and bracket access: arr?.[0], obj?.method(). Short-circuits the rest of the chain.

question_text: What is the nullish coalescing operator (??)?
expected_answer: Returns the right side only when left is null or undefined, unlike || which triggers for all falsy values. const x = value ?? 'default' safely handles 0 or empty string as valid values.

question_text: What are JavaScript array methods and which are immutable?
expected_answer: Mutable: push, pop, shift, unshift, splice, sort, reverse, fill. Immutable (return new array): map, filter, reduce, slice, concat, flat, flatMap, find, findIndex, some, every.

question_text: What is Array.prototype.reduce() and give a use case?
expected_answer: reduce(callback, initialValue) accumulates values: sum: arr.reduce((acc, n) => acc + n, 0). Also used for grouping: reduce into object, flattening arrays, and counting occurrences.

question_text: What is Array.prototype.find() vs Array.prototype.filter()?
expected_answer: find() returns the first matching element (or undefined). filter() returns an array of all matching elements. find() is more efficient when you need only the first match.

question_text: What is Array.from() in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Array.from() creates a new array from an iterable or array-like object (NodeList, string, Map, Set). Also accepts a map function: Array.from({length:5}, (_, i) => i).

question_text: What is the JavaScript Symbol type?
expected_answer: Symbol creates unique, immutable primitive values as object property keys to avoid name collisions. Symbol('desc') === Symbol('desc') is false. Used for well-known symbols like Symbol.iterator.

question_text: What is Object.freeze() in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Object.freeze() makes an object immutable: no adding, deleting, or modifying properties. Shallow (nested objects can still be mutated). Use for constants or immutable state.

question_text: What is Object.assign() vs spread in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Both do shallow copy/merge. Object.assign(target, ...sources) mutates the target. Spread { ...obj1, ...obj2 } creates a new object. Spread is preferred for immutability.

question_text: What is the JavaScript error types?
expected_answer: Built-in errors: Error (base), TypeError (wrong type), ReferenceError (undefined variable), SyntaxError (parse error), RangeError (out of bounds), URIError, EvalError.

question_text: What is error handling with try/catch/finally?
expected_answer: try block runs code. catch(err) handles thrown errors. finally always runs (cleanup). throw creates custom errors: throw new Error('message'). catch receives the error object.

question_text: What is debouncing and how do you implement it?
expected_answer: Debounce delays execution until after a period of inactivity: function debounce(fn, delay) { let timer; return (...args) => { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(() => fn(...args), delay) } }.

question_text: What is throttling and how is it different from debouncing?
expected_answer: Throttle limits to max one call per interval: last time tracked, call only if enough time passed. Debounce waits for silence. Throttle for regular intervals (scroll), debounce for final state (search).

question_text: What is memoization in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Memoization caches function results for given inputs, returning cached value on repeated calls. Implemented with a closure and Map/object as cache. Improves performance for expensive pure functions.

question_text: What is the JavaScript generator function?
expected_answer: function* with yield creates a generator producing lazy values on demand. Each .next() call runs until the next yield. Used for infinite sequences, pagination, and custom iterables.

question_text: What is the Proxy object in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Proxy wraps an object, intercepting operations via handler traps (get, set, deleteProperty, has). Used for validation, reactivity systems (Vue 3), logging, and access control.

question_text: What is the WeakMap and when to use it?
expected_answer: WeakMap holds weak references to object keys, allowing garbage collection. Use for private data storage on objects (class private state) without preventing GC when the object is no longer needed.

question_text: What is the Intersection Observer API and how is it used?
expected_answer: IntersectionObserver(callback, options) observes visibility of elements: new IntersectionObserver((entries) => { entries.forEach(entry => { if(entry.isIntersecting) { /* lazy load */ } }) }).

question_text: What is the requestAnimationFrame API?
expected_answer: rAF schedules a callback before the next repaint, synced to the display refresh rate (~60fps). Optimal for animations: function animate() { update(); requestAnimationFrame(animate) }.

question_text: What is the History API in JavaScript?
expected_answer: pushState(state, title, url) adds history without reload. replaceState() modifies current entry. popstate event fires on back/forward navigation. Enables SPA routing with real URLs.

question_text: What is the Clipboard API in JavaScript?
expected_answer: navigator.clipboard.writeText(text) copies to clipboard (returns Promise). navigator.clipboard.readText() reads clipboard. Requires HTTPS and user permission.

question_text: What is the Geolocation API?
expected_answer: navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(success, error) gets user's current position. watchPosition() continuously updates. Requires user permission and HTTPS.

question_text: What is performance optimization for frontend?
expected_answer: Key optimizations: minimize/compress JS/CSS, lazy-load images, code-split, use CDN, cache assets, reduce render-blocking resources, optimize fonts, minimize DOM operations, and use requestAnimationFrame for animations.

question_text: What is the CSS paint API / Houdini?
expected_answer: CSS Houdini exposes the browser rendering pipeline, allowing custom CSS properties, layout, paint, and animation worklets for extending CSS capabilities beyond what's natively available.

question_text: What is a CSS methodology and why is it useful?
expected_answer: CSS methodologies (BEM, SMACSS, OOCSS, Atomic CSS) provide naming conventions and organizational principles for scalable, maintainable stylesheets in team environments.

question_text: What is CSS specificity conflict and how do you resolve it without !important?
expected_answer: Increase specificity by adding more selectors, restructure HTML for better selector targeting, refactor to use CSS custom properties, or reorganize stylesheet order to take advantage of cascade.

question_text: What is the CSS paint order and stacking context?
expected_answer: Stacking contexts are created by position + z-index, opacity < 1, transform, filter, isolation: isolate. Elements in a stacking context are painted together, isolated from other contexts' z-index.

question_text: What is font loading optimization?
expected_answer: Use font-display:swap for text visibility during font load, preload critical fonts (<link rel='preload' as='font'>), subset fonts, use woff2 format, and system-ui fallback stacks.

question_text: What is the CSS font-display property?
expected_answer: font-display controls font swap behavior: swap (shows fallback, swaps when loaded), optional (uses fallback if font not cached), block (invisible text briefly), fallback (short block then swap).

question_text: What is the FOUT and FOIT problem in web fonts?
expected_answer: FOUT (Flash of Unstyled Text): fallback font shows, then swaps. FOIT (Flash of Invisible Text): text hidden until font loads. font-display:swap causes FOUT; font-display:block causes FOIT.

question_text: What is CSS specificity vs. source order?
expected_answer: When two rules have equal specificity, the later one in source order wins due to the cascade. This is why rule order in stylesheets and import order matter for predictable styling.

question_text: What is the :has() CSS pseudo-class?
expected_answer: :has() is a relational pseudo-class selecting parents containing specific children: article:has(img) selects articles containing images. First CSS ancestor selector, enabling truly powerful selectors.

question_text: What is the CSS text-decoration shorthand?
expected_answer: text-decoration shorthand: text-decoration: underline dotted red. Components: text-decoration-line (underline/overline/line-through), text-decoration-style (solid/dashed/dotted), text-decoration-color.

question_text: What is the CSS font-variant property?
expected_answer: font-variant enables OpenType features: small-caps, numeric formatting (font-variant-numeric), ligatures (font-variant-ligatures), providing typographic refinements without separate font files.

question_text: What is letter-spacing vs word-spacing in CSS?
expected_answer: letter-spacing adjusts space between individual characters. word-spacing adjusts space between words. Both accept em values relative to font-size for responsive typography.

question_text: What is the CSS white-space property?
expected_answer: white-space: normal (wraps), nowrap (no wrap), pre (preserves whitespace), pre-wrap (preserves whitespace + wraps), pre-line (collapses spaces but preserves newlines).

question_text: What is the difference between padding: 10px and padding: 10px 20px 15px 5px?
expected_answer: Single value applies to all sides. Two values: vertical horizontal. Three values: top horizontal bottom. Four values: top right bottom left (clockwise). Shorthand for padding-top/right/bottom/left.

question_text: What is the CSS resize property?
expected_answer: resize allows users to resize an element: none (default), both, horizontal, vertical. Requires overflow value other than visible to work. Used for resizable textareas.

question_text: What is the CSS outline-offset property?
expected_answer: outline-offset sets the space between the outline and the element's border. Positive values push outline outward; negative values draw inside the element. Useful for custom focus indicators.

question_text: What is tab-size in CSS?
expected_answer: tab-size sets the width (in spaces or length unit) of a tab character in pre-formatted text elements, controlling how indentation appears in <pre> and <code> elements.

question_text: What is the CSS isolation property?
expected_answer: isolation: isolate creates a new stacking context without requiring other properties (z-index, opacity, transform), preventing an element's contents from blending with elements behind it.

question_text: What is the CSS shape-outside property?
expected_answer: shape-outside defines a geometric shape around which inline content wraps (shape-outside: circle(50%) on floated element), enabling magazine-like text wrapping around irregular shapes.

question_text: What is React and what problem does it solve?
expected_answer: React is a JavaScript library for building component-based UIs. It solves the complexity of building interactive UIs by using a component model, virtual DOM diffing, and declarative rendering.

question_text: What is JSX and how does it compile?
expected_answer: JSX is JavaScript syntax extension looking like HTML. Babel compiles JSX to React.createElement() calls. JSX expressions must have one root element or use a Fragment (<> </> or React.Fragment).

question_text: What is a React functional component?
expected_answer: A functional component is a JavaScript function returning JSX: const Button = ({ label, onClick }) => <button onClick={onClick}>{label}</button>. The standard way to write React components.

question_text: What are React props and how are they used?
expected_answer: Props are read-only inputs passed to components as HTML attributes: <Button label='Click' onClick={fn} />. Received as an object parameter. Children are passed as props.children.

question_text: What is the useState hook in React?
expected_answer: const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue) manages local component state. setState(newValue) or setState(prev => newValue) triggers re-render. New state can be any type.

question_text: What is the useEffect hook and what is its dependency array?
expected_answer: useEffect(fn, deps) runs fn after render. Empty [] runs once on mount. [dep1, dep2] runs when deps change. No array runs after every render. Return cleanup function for unmount.

question_text: What is the virtual DOM in React?
expected_answer: React maintains a virtual DOM (lightweight JS representation of the real DOM). When state changes, React diffs new vs old virtual DOM (reconciliation) and only updates changed real DOM parts.

question_text: What are the rules of React hooks?
expected_answer: 1. Only call hooks at the top level (not inside loops, conditions, or nested functions). 2. Only call hooks from React functions (functional components or custom hooks).

question_text: What is the key prop in React and why is it important?
expected_answer: key is a unique identifier for list items helping React identify which items changed, added, or removed. Stable keys (IDs not indices) enable correct reconciliation and prevent state mixing.

question_text: What is React conditional rendering?
expected_answer: Conditional rendering shows different UI based on state/props: ternary ({isLoggedIn ? <A/> : <B/>}), short-circuit ({isLoggedIn && <A/>}), or extracted variables.

question_text: What is React list rendering and how do you do it?
expected_answer:
Map over an array to render list items, always providing a unique key: {items.map(item =>
  • {item.name}
    • )}. Keys must be stable and unique among siblings.

question_text: What is prop drilling in React?
expected_answer: Prop drilling passes data through multiple component layers that don't directly use it. Solved by Context API (for global data), Redux, or component composition to avoid unnecessary passes.

question_text: What is the React Context API?
expected_answer: Context provides a way to share values without prop drilling. createContext() creates context, Provider wraps components with value, useContext() hook consumes it in any descendant.

question_text: What is lifting state up in React?
expected_answer: Moving state to the nearest common ancestor so sibling components can share it via props. The parent holds state, passes it and update callbacks down to children.

question_text: What is React.memo and when should you use it?
expected_answer: React.memo wraps a component to memoize it, preventing re-render if props haven't shallowly changed. Use when a component re-renders unnecessarily due to parent re-renders with unchanged props.

question_text: What is the useCallback hook?
expected_answer: useCallback(fn, deps) memoizes a callback function, returning the same reference if deps unchanged. Prevents child components receiving callbacks as props from re-rendering unnecessarily.

question_text: What is the useMemo hook?
expected_answer: useMemo(fn, deps) memoizes an expensive computed value, recalculating only when deps change. Use for heavy calculations or filtering/sorting large arrays to avoid repeated computation.

question_text: What is the useRef hook in React?
expected_answer: useRef() returns a mutable ref object with .current property. Used for DOM references (element.focus()), storing mutable values that don't trigger re-renders (timers, previous values).

question_text: What is the difference between useEffect and useLayoutEffect?
expected_answer: useEffect runs asynchronously after the browser paints. useLayoutEffect runs synchronously after DOM mutations but before paint, suitable for DOM measurements to avoid flicker.

question_text: What is a controlled form in React?
expected_answer: A controlled form binds input value to React state and updates via onChange: <input value={value} onChange={e => setValue(e.target.value)} />. React is the single source of truth for form data.

question_text: What is code splitting in React?
expected_answer: Code splitting lazily loads parts of the app on demand using React.lazy(() => import('./Component')) wrapped in <Suspense fallback={<Loading/>}>, reducing initial bundle size.

question_text: What is a React Fragment?
expected_answer: Fragment (<> </> or <React.Fragment>) groups multiple elements without adding an extra DOM node, useful when a component must return multiple elements without a wrapping div.

question_text: What is the difference between a class component and a functional component in React?
expected_answer: Class components use lifecycle methods and this.state. Functional components use hooks for state and side effects, are simpler, and are the modern React standard. Hooks cannot be used in class components.

question_text: What is React Router and how do you set up basic routing?
expected_answer: React Router v6: wrap app in <BrowserRouter>, use <Routes> with <Route path='/about' element={<About/>}> for route definitions, and <Link to='/about'> for navigation.

question_text: What is the useNavigate hook in React Router?
expected_answer: useNavigate() returns a function to programmatically navigate: const navigate = useNavigate(); navigate('/home') navigates, navigate(-1) goes back.

question_text: What is the useParams hook in React Router?
expected_answer: useParams() returns an object of URL parameters defined in the Route path. For <Route path='/users/:id'>, useParams().id gives the dynamic segment value.

question_text: What is the React reconciliation algorithm?
expected_answer: React's reconciler (Fiber) diffs virtual DOM trees: same type = update, different type = replace. Keys help identify list items. Minimal DOM operations are batched for efficiency.

question_text: What is batching in React?
expected_answer: Batching groups multiple setState calls into a single re-render for performance. React 18 introduced automatic batching for async operations, Promises, setTimeout, not just event handlers.

question_text: What is the StrictMode in React?
expected_answer: <React.StrictMode> wraps the app in development to detect side effects, deprecated APIs, and unexpected behavior by intentionally double-invoking certain functions. Has no effect in production.

question_text: What is a custom React hook?
expected_answer: A custom hook is a function starting with 'use' that extracts reusable stateful logic: function useFetch(url) { const [data, setData] = useState(null); useEffect(()=>{...}, [url]); return data }.

question_text: What is the useReducer hook in React?
expected_answer: useReducer(reducer, initialState) manages complex state with (state, action) => newState pattern. dispatch(action) triggers state updates. Better than useState for complex interdependent state.

question_text: What are browser developer tools and how are they used?
expected_answer: DevTools (F12): Elements (inspect/edit DOM+CSS), Console (JS REPL), Network (HTTP requests), Performance (profiling), Sources (debugger), Application (storage/PWA), Accessibility.

question_text: What is the browser console and what methods are available?
expected_answer: Console methods: log (info), warn (yellow warning), error (red error), table (tabular data), group/groupEnd (collapsible groups), time/timeEnd (measure duration), assert (conditional error).

question_text: What is a CSS reset and why use it?
expected_answer: A CSS reset (or normalize) removes browser-default inconsistencies in margins, padding, and typography, providing a clean consistent base for styling across all browsers.

question_text: What is cross-browser compatibility in frontend development?
expected_answer: Cross-browser compatibility ensures the site works correctly in all major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge). Requires testing, feature detection (Modernizr), polyfills, and avoiding browser-specific APIs.

question_text: What is a polyfill in web development?
expected_answer: A polyfill provides modern functionality in older browsers that don't natively support it. Examples: core-js for Promise/Array.from, IntersectionObserver polyfill, CSS custom properties polyfill.

question_text: What is progressive enhancement?
expected_answer: Progressive enhancement builds from a baseline of core HTML functionality, adding CSS for styling and JavaScript for interactivity as layers. Ensures usability even when CSS/JS fails.

question_text: What is graceful degradation?
expected_answer: Graceful degradation builds fully-featured for modern browsers and ensures the site still works (though with reduced features) on older browsers. Opposite approach to progressive enhancement.

question_text: What are CSS vendor prefixes and why are they needed?
expected_answer: Vendor prefixes (-webkit-, -moz-, -ms-) were used by browsers for experimental CSS features. Autoprefixer adds them automatically. Modern CSS features rarely need prefixes.

question_text: What is the CSS :where() pseudo-class?
expected_answer: :where() groups selectors like :is() but with zero specificity, useful for base styles that can easily be overridden: :where(h1, h2, h3) { line-height: 1.2 } can be overridden with just h2 {}.

question_text: What is the difference between CSS Grid implicit and explicit tracks?
expected_answer: Explicit tracks are defined by grid-template-columns/rows. Implicit tracks are created automatically for extra items, sized by grid-auto-rows/columns (default: auto).

question_text: What is place-items in CSS Grid?
expected_answer: place-items is a shorthand for align-items and justify-items in Grid: place-items: center centers items both vertically and horizontally in their grid cells.

question_text: What is the difference between align-items and align-content in CSS?
expected_answer: align-items aligns flex/grid items within their row/track on the cross axis. align-content distributes multiple rows/tracks when there's extra space on the cross axis.

question_text: What is the CSS padding-inline and padding-block (logical properties)?
expected_answer: Logical properties use flow-relative directions: padding-inline sets start and end padding (left/right in LTR), padding-block sets top/bottom. Supports RTL layouts without separate CSS.

question_text: What is the CSS color-scheme property?
expected_answer: color-scheme: light dark declares that the component accepts both color schemes, allowing browsers to style native form elements, scrollbars, and system colors appropriately for the current mode.

question_text: What is the prefers-color-scheme media query?
expected_answer: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) applies styles when the user has selected a dark color scheme in OS settings, enabling automatic dark mode support.

question_text: What is the prefers-reduced-motion media query?
expected_answer: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) applies styles for users who have requested reduced motion in OS settings, allowing disabling of non-essential animations for accessibility.

question_text: What is focus management for accessibility?
expected_answer: Focus management ensures keyboard users can navigate: visible focus indicators, logical tab order, managing focus when modals open/close (trap focus inside, restore on close), and skip navigation links.

question_text: What is a skip navigation link?
expected_answer: A visually hidden link (shown on focus) allowing keyboard users to skip repetitive navigation and jump directly to main content: Skip to main content.

question_text: What is color contrast and WCAG guidelines?
expected_answer: WCAG 2.1 requires minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio for normal text, 3:1 for large text (AA level). 7:1 for AAA. Tools: Chrome DevTools, Colour Contrast Analyser, axe DevTools.

question_text: What is the role attribute in ARIA?
expected_answer: role attribute overrides or clarifies the semantic meaning of an element: role='button' on a div, role='dialog' on a modal, role='navigation', role='alert' for dynamic announcements.

question_text: What is live region in ARIA?
expected_answer: aria-live regions announce dynamic content changes to screen readers: aria-live='polite' (waits for current speech), aria-live='assertive' (interrupts). Used for status messages and form errors.

question_text: What is the difference between HTML validation and form validation?
expected_answer: HTML validation uses built-in attributes (required, pattern, min, max) and the Constraint Validation API. Form validation (JavaScript-based) provides custom error messages and complex validation logic.

question_text: What is the CSS :valid and :invalid pseudo-class?
expected_answer: :valid styles form inputs passing HTML validation constraints. :invalid styles failing inputs. Combine with :user-invalid (modern) to only show errors after user interaction, not immediately.

question_text: What is CSS specificity when using :not() pseudo-class?
expected_answer: :not() specificity is based on its argument's specificity. :not(.active) has class-level specificity (0,0,1,0). :not(#id) has ID-level specificity. The :not itself adds no specificity.

question_text: What is the difference between inline styles and CSS classes?
expected_answer: Inline styles (style='') have highest specificity (1000), no reusability, harder to maintain. CSS classes are reusable, maintainable, respect cascade, and separate concerns. Use classes except for dynamic values.

question_text: What is the CSS min() and max() function?
expected_answer: min(a, b) returns the smaller value: font-size: min(5vw, 2rem) prevents text from growing too large. max(a, b) returns the larger: width: max(300px, 50%) ensures minimum width.

question_text: What is the CSS env() function?
expected_answer: env() accesses CSS environment variables defined by the browser, especially safe-area-inset-* for iOS notch/home indicator: padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) for iPhone safe areas.

question_text: What is CSS Containment?
expected_answer: contain property limits an element's rendering scope: contain: layout (layout changes don't affect outside), paint (no overflow), size (size independent), style. Improves performance of isolated components.

question_text: What is JavaScript strict mode?
expected_answer: 'use strict' enables strict mode: prevents undeclared variables, disallows duplicate parameters, this is undefined (not global) in regular functions, reserves future keywords.

question_text: What is the difference between a deep copy and shallow copy of an object in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Shallow copy (spread, Object.assign) copies top-level properties; nested objects remain shared references. Deep copy (structuredClone, recursive copy) creates fully independent nested copies.

question_text: What is event.stopImmediatePropagation()?
expected_answer: stopImmediatePropagation() stops bubbling AND prevents other handlers on the same element from firing, unlike stopPropagation() which allows other handlers on the current element to run.

question_text: What is the difference between a forEach and for...of loop?
expected_answer: forEach is an array method with callback, no break/continue support, skips holes. for...of works on any iterable (arrays, Sets, Maps, generators), supports break/continue, and is more flexible.

question_text: What is the JavaScript Number type limitation?
expected_answer: JavaScript uses 64-bit IEEE 754 floating-point (doubles). Max safe integer: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (2^53-1). Beyond this, integers lose precision. Use BigInt for larger numbers.

question_text: What is BigInt in JavaScript?
expected_answer: BigInt represents integers beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER: 9007199254740993n. Append n suffix or use BigInt(). Cannot be mixed with Number in operations. Useful for precise large integer arithmetic.

question_text: What is the CSS overscroll-behavior property?
expected_answer: overscroll-behavior: contain prevents scroll chaining (parent scroll triggered after child reaches end). none removes all overscroll effects including pull-to-refresh on mobile.

question_text: What is CSS logical properties and when to use them?
expected_answer: Logical properties (margin-inline-start, padding-block-end) use flow-relative directions instead of physical (left/right/top/bottom), automatically adapting to writing-mode and dir attribute.

question_text: What is CSS named color and currentColor?
expected_answer: currentColor is a CSS keyword representing the current element's color value, usable in other properties: border: 1px solid currentColor. Enables consistent color theming.

question_text: What is the CSS inherit, initial, and unset keywords?
expected_answer: inherit: forces inheritance from parent. initial: resets to CSS specification default. unset: acts as inherit for inherited properties, initial for non-inherited properties.

question_text: What is the CSS revert keyword?
expected_answer: revert rolls back a property to the browser's default stylesheet value (user-agent default), preserving inherited values. Different from initial which resets to specification default.

question_text: What is the CSS layer (@layer) rule?
expected_answer: @layer creates explicit cascade layers allowing fine-grained control of specificity order. Styles in lower-declared layers lose to higher-declared ones regardless of specificity, enabling predictable overrides.

question_text: What is Flexbox gap vs margin?
expected_answer: gap (row-gap, column-gap) adds spacing only between flex/grid items, not on outer edges. margin adds space around every item including outer edges. gap is cleaner for gutters.

question_text: What is the aspect-ratio CSS property?
expected_answer: aspect-ratio: 16/9 maintains the element's proportional width to height. Used for responsive videos, images, and UI components that should maintain a consistent shape regardless of size.

question_text: What is the CSS line-clamp technique?
expected_answer: display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 3; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden truncates text to N lines with ellipsis. The standard line-clamp property is upcoming.

question_text: What is the ResizeObserver API?
expected_answer: ResizeObserver(callback) monitors element size changes, firing when content or border box dimensions change. More accurate than window resize events for element-level responsiveness.

question_text: What is the MutationObserver API?
expected_answer: MutationObserver observes DOM changes: added/removed children, attribute changes, text node changes. More efficient than polling for detecting third-party DOM modifications.

question_text: What is the difference between absolute and fixed positioning?
expected_answer: absolute positions relative to the nearest non-static ancestor, scrolls with page. fixed positions relative to the viewport, stays in place during scroll. Both are out of normal flow.

question_text: What is the CSS perspective property?
expected_answer: perspective adds 3D depth to child elements. Set on parent: perspective: 500px. The smaller the value, the more dramatic the 3D effect. Required for 3D CSS transforms (rotateX, rotateY).

question_text: What is the CSS transform: translate vs position change for animation?
expected_answer: transform: translate is GPU-composited and doesn't trigger layout or paint, making it the most performant way to animate position. Changing top/left triggers layout (expensive reflow).

question_text: What are CSS layers of rendering performance?
expected_answer: Render layers: JavaScript → Style → Layout → Paint → Composite. Compositing (transform, opacity) is fastest. Triggering layout (top, left, width) is most expensive. Target compositor properties for smooth animation.

question_text: What is the CSS content-visibility property?
expected_answer: content-visibility: auto skips rendering of off-screen content entirely, significantly improving initial render performance for long pages by deferring layout and paint until near-scroll.

question_text: What are web fonts best practices?
expected_answer: Preload critical fonts, use woff2 format, set font-display:swap, limit font weights/variants, self-host for GDPR compliance, use system font stacks as fallbacks, and subset fonts.

question_text: What is a CSS card component pattern?
expected_answer: A card uses display:flex/grid, border-radius, box-shadow, overflow:hidden, and responsive sizing. Inner content uses Flexbox for equal-height columns and proper spacing with gap.

question_text: What is the CSS ::marker pseudo-element?
expected_answer: ::marker styles the bullet or number of list items: li::marker { color: red; font-size: 1.5em }. Allows custom list marker styling without replacing the semantic list element.

question_text: What is the CSS :focus-within pseudo-class?
expected_answer: :focus-within matches an element when it or any of its descendants has focus. Useful for showing label styles or wrappers when any child input is focused.

question_text: What is the CSS :empty pseudo-class?
expected_answer: :empty matches elements with no children (including text nodes). Useful for hiding empty containers: .notification:empty { display: none } avoids empty placeholder UI.

question_text: What is the CSS counter-reset and counter-increment?
expected_answer: counter-reset creates/resets a named counter on an element. counter-increment increases it on target elements. counter() in content: displays the value in ::before/::after.

question_text: What is the difference between border-radius: 50% and border-radius: 100px?
expected_answer: 50% creates a circle/ellipse relative to element dimensions, adapting to size changes. 100px applies a fixed corner radius. For circular images of unknown size, 50% is preferred.

question_text: What is the CSS grid auto-placement algorithm?
expected_answer: Grid auto-placement fills cells in order by default (row-by-row). grid-auto-flow: column changes to column-by-column. dense fills holes by rearranging items. Explicit placement overrides auto.

question_text: What is the CSS clipping vs masking?
expected_answer: clip-path clips with geometric shapes or SVG (hard edges). mask-image masks with image/gradient alpha channel (soft edges). Both hide parts outside the clipping/mask region.

question_text: What is the difference between :first-child and :first-of-type?
expected_answer: :first-child selects an element that is the first child of its parent. :first-of-type selects the first element of that specific type among siblings, regardless of position.

question_text: What is image lazy loading in HTML?
expected_answer: defers loading images until they approach the viewport, reducing initial page weight and improving LCP. loading='eager' forces immediate loading. No JavaScript needed.

question_text: What is the decoding attribute on img?
expected_answer: decoding='async' tells the browser to decode the image asynchronously, avoiding blocking other content rendering. decoding='sync' forces synchronous decoding (may block rendering).

question_text: What is the crossorigin attribute in HTML?
expected_answer: crossorigin='anonymous' or 'use-credentials' on script/link/img enables CORS for the resource, required for scripts loaded from CDNs to get proper error messages in onerror handlers.

question_text: What is the nonce attribute in HTML script tags?
expected_answer: A nonce (number used once) is a random value added to trusted inline scripts matching a Content-Security-Policy nonce directive, allowing inline scripts while blocking injected scripts.

question_text: What is the CSS overflow-x and overflow-y?
expected_answer: overflow-x and overflow-y control clipping independently for horizontal and vertical directions. overflow-x: auto with overflow-y: visible has browser quirks since both are set together.

question_text: What is touch action in CSS?
expected_answer: touch-action controls how the browser handles touch gestures: none (prevent all), pan-x (allow horizontal panning only), pan-y, pinch-zoom, manipulation. Used to prevent default scroll during custom gesture handling.

question_text: What is the CSS column layout (multi-column)?
expected_answer: column-count and column-width create newspaper-style multi-column layouts. column-gap controls spacing. column-rule adds visual separator. column-span: all makes an element span all columns.

question_text: What is the JavaScript AbortController?
expected_answer: AbortController provides an abort signal to cancel fetch requests: const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, {signal: controller.signal}); controller.abort() cancels the request.

question_text: What is the difference between HTTP GET and POST requests in JavaScript fetch?
expected_answer: GET: fetch(url) - no body, cached, bookmarkable. POST: fetch(url, {method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify(data)}) sends data in request body.

question_text: What is JavaScript error boundaries concept (without React)?
expected_answer: In vanilla JS, wrap operations in try/catch and use window.onerror or window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', handler) for global error handling of uncaught errors and Promise rejections.

question_text: What is the CSS writing in terms of scalability best practices?
expected_answer: Scalable CSS: low specificity, modular (BEM/CSS Modules), use custom properties, minimize !important, meaningful naming, separate layout from theme, and document complex selectors.

question_text: What is the difference between :nth-child(even) and :nth-child(2n)?
expected_answer: They are equivalent. :nth-child(even) = :nth-child(2n). An+B formula: A=step, B=offset. Examples: 3n+1 (every 3rd starting from 1st), odd = 2n+1.

question_text: What is the CSS orphans and widows property?
expected_answer: orphans sets minimum lines of a paragraph at the bottom of a print page. widows sets minimum lines at the top of the next page. Used for print CSS to avoid single-line danglers.

question_text: What is the print CSS and @media print?
expected_answer: @media print applies styles only when printing: hide navigation, remove backgrounds, show link URLs (a::after { content: ' (' attr(href) ')' }), adjust font sizes and page breaks.

question_text: What is the difference between SVG and icon fonts?
expected_answer: SVG icons are resolution-independent, colorable per icon, accessible (with title/desc), no blocking render. Icon fonts load as a font, can flicker, harder to style per icon, but widely supported.

question_text: What is the CSS text-rendering property?
expected_answer: text-rendering: optimizeLegibility enables ligatures and kerning at the cost of performance. optimizeSpeed disables them. geometricPrecision ensures consistent metrics for animations.

question_text: What is the CSS subgrid?
expected_answer: subgrid allows a grid item to participate in its parent grid's row/column definitions: grid-column: subgrid, enabling nested components to align to the outer grid tracks.

question_text: What is the CSS :placeholder-shown pseudo-class?
expected_answer: :placeholder-shown selects input elements when their placeholder text is visible (field is empty), useful for floating label animations without JavaScript.

question_text: What is the CSS all shorthand?
expected_answer: all: unset resets all CSS properties to their inherited or initial values. all: revert resets to user-agent styles. Useful for resetting component styles or iframe content.

question_text: What is the CSS caret-color property?
expected_answer: caret-color sets the color of the text input caret (blinking cursor) in inputs and contenteditable elements, enabling brand-consistent cursor styling.

question_text: What is the difference between display:flex and display:inline-flex?
expected_answer: display:flex creates a block-level flex container. display:inline-flex creates an inline-level container (sits in text flow), both creating a flex formatting context for their children.

question_text: What is the CSS inset shorthand?
expected_answer: inset is shorthand for top, right, bottom, left: inset: 0 is equivalent to top:0; right:0; bottom:0; left:0. Used with position:absolute/fixed for full coverage.

question_text: What is the JavaScript performance.now() API?
expected_answer: performance.now() returns a high-resolution timestamp (microseconds) since navigation start, unaffected by system clock changes. Used for accurate performance timing of code execution.

question_text: What is a JavaScript polyfill vs transpilation?
expected_answer: A polyfill adds missing runtime features (Promise, Array.from) to the environment. Transpilation (Babel) converts newer syntax (arrow functions, classes) to older syntax at build time.

question_text: What is the purpose of a CSS reset vs defensive CSS?
expected_answer: CSS reset removes browser defaults for a clean slate. Defensive CSS avoids relying on browser defaults by explicitly setting critical properties (overflow, box-sizing, white-space) to prevent layout breaks.

question_text: What is image compression and why is it important for performance?
expected_answer: Image compression (lossless: PNG, WebP; lossy: JPEG, WebP) reduces file size without (or with minimal) quality loss, improving load time, reducing bandwidth, and improving LCP score.

question_text: What are Core Web Vitals and why are they important?
expected_answer: Core Web Vitals measure user experience: LCP (loading), FID/INP (interactivity), CLS (visual stability). Used by Google as ranking signals since 2021, making them critical for SEO and UX.

question_text: What is the JavaScript PerformanceObserver API?
expected_answer: PerformanceObserver monitors performance metrics (LCP, FID, layout shift, resource timing) in real-time: new PerformanceObserver((list) => { ... }).observe({type: 'largest-contentful-paint'}).

question_text: What is tree shaking and how does it reduce bundle size?
expected_answer: Tree shaking statically analyzes ES module imports to identify and eliminate unused code. Works with named exports and side-effect-free modules. Enabled in Webpack (mode: production) and Rollup.

question_text: What is the CSS :defined pseudo-class?
expected_answer: :defined matches elements that have been defined (both built-in elements and custom elements that have been registered), useful for styling before/after custom element registration.

question_text: What is a Web Component?
expected_answer: Web Components are a set of native browser APIs: Custom Elements (define new HTML elements), Shadow DOM (scoped DOM + CSS), and HTML Templates (<template>) for reusable UI components without frameworks.

question_text: What is Shadow DOM?
expected_answer: Shadow DOM creates an encapsulated DOM tree attached to an element, with scoped CSS that doesn't leak in or out. Used in Web Components to create isolated, reusable UI components.

question_text: What is the CSS all: unset use case?
expected_answer: all: unset is used to strip all inherited and applied styles from an element, creating a clean slate for custom component styling without battling inherited or global CSS rules.

question_text: What is the HTML template element?
expected_answer: <template> contains HTML that isn't rendered immediately but can be cloned and inserted via JavaScript (template.content.cloneNode(true)), enabling reusable HTML snippets without rendering overhead.

question_text: What is the JavaScript structuredClone() function?
expected_answer: structuredClone(obj) creates a deep clone handling Date, Map, Set, RegExp, ArrayBuffer, and circular references — things JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()) cannot handle.

question_text: What is input type=number vs input type=text for numeric input?
expected_answer: type=number shows numeric keyboard on mobile, has min/max/step validation, but has quirks (trailing zeros stripped, e allowed). type=text with pattern='[0-9]*' gives better control for formatted numbers.

question_text: What is the CSS grid-template shorthand?
expected_answer: grid-template combines grid-template-rows, grid-template-columns, and grid-template-areas: grid-template: 'header header' 80px / 200px 1fr defines named areas with explicit sizing.

question_text: What is the difference between a design token and a CSS variable?
expected_answer: Design tokens are platform-agnostic named values (color-primary: #007bff). CSS variables (--color-primary: #007bff) are CSS-specific implementations of tokens. Tokens can generate CSS variables, iOS constants, etc.

question_text: What is the CSS appearance:none hack for checkboxes?
expected_answer: appearance:none removes native checkbox/radio styling. Then use ::before/::after with custom CSS to build custom styled checkboxes while keeping native HTML semantics and keyboard/form functionality.

question_text: What is the purpose of the HTML lang attribute?
expected_answer: lang attribute on <html> specifies the document's language (lang='en'), enabling screen readers to use correct pronunciation, search engines to index correctly, and spell-checkers to use the right dictionary.

question_text: What is the HTML dir attribute?
expected_answer: dir='ltr' or 'rtl' sets text direction left-to-right or right-to-left. dir='auto' detects from content. Used with lang for proper bidirectional text rendering in Arabic, Hebrew.

question_text: What is the CSS font-size-adjust property?
expected_answer: font-size-adjust maintains consistent x-height when fonts fallback, preventing visible size jumps when the preferred font isn't loaded and a fallback with different metrics is used.

question_text: What is the difference between aria-expanded and aria-controls?
expected_answer: aria-expanded indicates whether a collapsible element (accordion, dropdown) is expanded (true) or collapsed (false). aria-controls references the ID of the element it controls/reveals.
