question_text: What is the CSS text-size-adjust property?
expected_answer: text-size-adjust: 100% (or none) prevents mobile browsers from automatically inflating text size on small screens. Used to maintain intended typography on mobile without interference.

question_text: What is the CSS table-layout property?
expected_answer: table-layout: auto (default, column width based on content) vs fixed (column width based on first row only, more predictable performance). Use fixed with width: 100% for fast table rendering.

question_text: What is image decoding optimization in frontend?
expected_answer: Use loading='lazy' for below-fold images, decoding='async' to avoid blocking paint, explicit width/height to prevent CLS, WebP/AVIF formats, and proper srcset for responsive delivery.

question_text: What is JavaScript optional chaining with methods?
expected_answer: obj?.method() calls method only if obj exists. obj?.items?.[0]?.name accesses nested array item safely. Prevents TypeError when chaining through potentially null/undefined values.

question_text: What is a pure function in JavaScript?
expected_answer: A pure function always returns the same output for the same input and has no side effects (doesn't modify external state). Enables predictability, testability, and memoization.

question_text: What is the difference between Array.some() and Array.every()?
expected_answer: some() returns true if at least one element passes the test (short-circuits on first true). every() returns true only if all elements pass (short-circuits on first false).

question_text: What is the JavaScript includes() vs indexOf()?
expected_answer: includes() returns a boolean: arr.includes(NaN) works correctly. indexOf() returns index or -1, but indexOf(NaN) returns -1 (NaN !== NaN issue). Use includes() for membership testing.

question_text: What is event.composedPath() in JavaScript?
expected_answer: composedPath() returns an array of all elements the event propagated through from target to window, including elements inside Shadow DOM, enabling cross-shadow-root event delegation.

question_text: What is the CSS var() fallback value?
expected_answer: var(--color, #000) uses the custom property if defined, otherwise falls back to the second argument #000. Fallback can be another var(): var(--primary, var(--brand, blue)).

question_text: What is the CSS :focus pseudo-class vs :focus-visible?
expected_answer: :focus applies to any focused element (via mouse or keyboard). :focus-visible applies only for keyboard focus (where the focus ring is actually needed for usability/accessibility).

question_text: What is the HTML5 video element and its attributes?
expected_answer: <video src='url' controls autoplay muted loop poster='img.jpg'> embeds video. Attributes: controls (native UI), autoplay (requires muted), muted, loop, poster (thumbnail), preload.

question_text: What is the HTML5 audio element?
expected_answer: <audio src='url' controls> embeds audio. Multiple <source> children provide format fallbacks. Accessible with proper labels and transcripts for deaf users.

question_text: What is the CSS aspect-ratio for video containers?
expected_answer: aspect-ratio: 16/9 on a container with position:relative and iframe/video set to width:100%;height:100% (or position:absolute;inset:0) creates a responsive video wrapper without padding-top hack.

question_text: What is lazy evaluation in JavaScript?
expected_answer: Lazy evaluation defers computation until the value is actually needed. Implemented via generators (yield), getters (computed on access), and || / && short-circuit operators.

question_text: What is CSS Modules?
expected_answer: CSS Modules scope class names locally by transforming them into unique identifiers at build time, preventing global CSS conflicts. Import as object: import styles from './Component.module.css'.

question_text: What is critical CSS and how to implement it?
expected_answer: Critical CSS is the minimum CSS for above-fold rendering, inlined in <head> for fast first paint. Generated by tools (Critical, Penthouse), full CSS loaded asynchronously via JS or preload+media trick.

question_text: What is a render-blocking resource?
expected_answer: Render-blocking resources (CSS in <head>, sync scripts) pause HTML parsing/rendering until downloaded+parsed. Fix by deferring scripts (defer/async), inlining critical CSS, and preloading key resources.

question_text: What is the CSS border-image property?
expected_answer: border-image slices an image into nine regions to fill as a border, enabling complex decorative borders. Shorthand: border-image: url(border.png) 30 round, with slice/width/outset/repeat.

question_text: What is the HTML slot element and Shadow DOM?
expected_answer: <slot> inside Shadow DOM creates insertion points where light DOM children are rendered. Named slots (<slot name='title'>) allow distributing specific children into specific positions in a Web Component.
